review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Round monetary results with the project's money helper
item.description: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected for violating the team's rounding convention.
item.content: When a function returns a money amount, wrap the final value in the repository's rounding helper (e.g. ledgerly.money.round_money) rather than returning a raw Decimal division or using Python's round()/quantize(), which use banker's rounding.

item.title: Read the money module before implementing money logic
item.description: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py revealed ZERO, round_money and to_money, which the accepted solution reused.
item.content: Before writing arithmetic on prices or totals, open the project's money module and reuse its constants and helpers (ZERO, to_money, round_money) so behavior matches existing functions like line_total and invoice_total.

item.title: Guard division by zero for empty collections
item.description: The weighted average must return zero when the invoice has no lines or zero total quantity.
item.content: Compute the denominator first and return the zero constant early when it is falsy, then perform the weighted sum with an explicit ZERO start value so empty inputs never raise ZeroDivisionError.
